div.head: Cn 1020 4
div.ab: Nu ne wandode ic na minum sceattum, þa hwile þe eow unfrið on handa stod; nu ic mid Godes fultume þæt totwæmde mid minum scattum.
Nu ne wandode ic na minum sceattum, þa hwile þe eow unfrið on handa stod; nu ic mid Godes fultume þæt totwæmde mid minum scattum.
[2] Nu ne wandode ic na minum sceattum þa hwile þe eow unfrið on handa stod; nu ic mid Godes fultume þæt totwæmde mid minum scattum.
Nun sparte ich meine Schätze nicht, dieweil euch politische Unruhe vorhanden war; nun hab ich mit Gottes Hilfe dies durch meine Schätze beigelegt.
Now I did not spare my treasure while hostility was upon you; now with God's help I have put an end to it with my treasure.
Recently I did not spare my money when hostility was threatening you, and now, with the help of God, I have averted it with my money.
Now that I have not spared my money as long as hostility was threatening you, I have with God’s help put an end to it with my money.
Now then, I did not withhold my money when a threat to you was at hand; now with God’s help, I have dispersed it with my wealth.
div.note: [2] a threat to you: It is unclear what the proclamation refers to here. to Denmark: Cnut’s trip to Denmark is recorded in the 1019 and 1020 entries in the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

note.seg: Cnuts äussere Erfolge waren mehrfach mit Geld erkauft (Encom. Emmae p. 520); durch Bestechung gewann er 1029 Norwegen; Steenstrup Normannerne III 357. Doch scheint, ebenso wie in 5, hier unter unfrið Beunruhigung innerhalb Englands durch Dänen und der daraus folgende innere Zwist gemeint. Die Heimfahrt der Dänenschiffe steht beim Annalisten gleich hinter (und, wie es scheint, auch stilistisch verbunden mit) dem riesigen Dänengeld von 82500 ℔ und gleich vor dem Verfassung gebenden Reichstag zu Oxford 1018. Das Dänengeld bezahlte jene Wikinger. Ward es von Cnut, als dem Lande nicht ganz aufzubringen möglich, teilweise aus seinem Privat- und Kronschatz ergänzt? Oder nannte er die Staatseinkünfte seine eigenen? Vielleicht hatte er daneben seine Hingabe dreier Herzogtümer Ostanglien, Mercien und Northumbrien an drei Fürsten 1017 im Sinne, die auf Beruhigung des Dänischen Elements abzielte und ein finanzielles Opfer der Krone bedeutete. Unten, 1027, 15 sagt er, sich und seine Mühe opfere er fürs Englische Volk

Cnut's external successes were several times bought with money (Encom. Emmae p. 520); by bribery he won Norway in 1029; Steenstrup Normannerne III 357. But here, just as in 5, unfrið seems to mean disturbance within England by Danes and the internal strife resulting from it. In the annalist the homeward voyage of the Danish ships comes immediately after (and, it seems, is also stylistically linked with) the enormous Danegeld of 82,500 pounds, and immediately before the constitution-giving assembly at Oxford in 1018. The Danegeld paid off those Vikings. Was it partly made up by Cnut from his private and crown treasure, since the country could not wholly raise it? Or did he call the state revenues his own? Perhaps he also had in mind his grant in 1017 of three earldoms, East Anglia, Mercia and Northumbria, to three princes, which aimed at pacifying the Danish element and meant a financial sacrifice by the Crown. Below, 1027, 15, he says that he sacrifices himself and his labour for the English people

Dies war vielleicht das für bellum aut inimicitias in Cn 1027, 14 vorliegende Wort, wo diese Stelle und c. 6 anklingen. In den Agsächs. Annalen bedeutet unfrið (s. Toller, Plummer s. v.) mehrfach die durch die Dänen innerhalb Englands verursachten Feindseligkeiten. — Statt ‘vorhanden war’ kann man freier übs.: ‘drohend stand’

This was perhaps the word underlying bellum aut inimicitias in Cn 1027, 14, where this passage and c. 6 are echoed. In the Anglo-Saxon Annals unfrið (see Toller, Plummer s. v.) several times means the hostilities caused by the Danes within England. — Instead of 'vorhanden war' ['was present'] one may translate more freely: 'drohend stand' ['stood threatening']
Nicht conj. ‘nachdem’ (Pauli, Steenstrup), wodurch übrigens das c. 5 Erzählte noch deutlicher chronologisch später als c. 4 erschiene
Not the conjunction 'nachdem' ['after'] (Pauli, Steenstrup), which incidentally would make what is narrated in c. 5 appear even more clearly to be chronologically later than c. 4
Vgl. I Cn 17, 2 aus VI Atr 25, 1. Der Gedanke und vielleicht der Ausdruck unfrið ic totwæmde scheint von Einfluss auf Schreiber D von I Cn Pro: Cnut frið gefæstnode ⁊ saca getwæmde
Cf. I Cn 17, 2 from VI Atr 25, 1. The idea, and perhaps the expression unfrið ic totwæmde, seems to have influenced scribe D of I Cn Pro: Cnut frið gefæstnode ⁊ saca getwæmde
